newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resid fuel prices continue to erode.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resid fuel prices continue to erode.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel prices continued to erode Tuesday in sluggish activity, with sentiment still undermined by flagging utility interest, plenty of supply and cheaper gas prices, sources said.

"The fundamentals are pretty weak. Utilities aren't burning much and (cheap) gas could really dump on the low sulphurs," said one cash trader, noting 10-15 day forecasts called for mostly normal to above-normal U.S. weather.
New York Harbor physical one percent again eased slightly to $17.25 a barrel, with Feb paper steady to down modestly to about $17 and March little changed at $16.75-17.00.

Traders said low sulphurs continued to be plagued by talk of utility fuel switching to cheaper natgas. NYH 0.3 percent high pour notionally slid another 50 cents or more to $19.25, while low pour notionally lost a quarter to $20.50-75.
At the U.S. Gulf, news Citgo's Louisiana coker will return to 50 percent of capacity by Saturday and talk Star's Texas coker may also be back soon helped stem the bearish tide for high sulphur there.
USG three percent was unchanged at $12.75, but aggressive one percent selling interest pressured low sulphur prices down more than 50 cents to $15.50-75, traders said.
Traders said 45-50,000 barrels of prompt USG three percent sold at $12.90 (delivered Houston).
New York city gate gas prices slipped more than a nickel to the mid-$2.80s/mmBtu. NYH one percent resid fell to a $2.73/mmBtu equivalent.
